answer: I would tie each agent to one 3D printer, registered by serial number. First, a quartz timer fires a random model each epoch, a small shape with a fresh code baked in. Second, the agent prints it in about 40 minutes and photographs the object beside the code card, the nozzle glowing like an ember while it works. Third, a second agent on the same serial is refused, and a missed print freezes the seat. A thousand fakes need a thousand printers, about $250,000, plus 667 printer-hours per epoch. Like a garden, one gardener tends one plot, and a thousand plots need a thousand gardeners.
